_description: Defines the runnable agent interaction that reconstructs Anderson & Holt (1997)'s sequential urn-prediction cascade task. The agent under test stands in, one decision at a time, for the human 'decision maker' role described in materials/materials.json: on every call it receives one private ball draw plus the public record of decisions already announced earlier in that period, and must announce an urn prediction (A or B). task/adapter.py implements the surrounding simulation (die rolls, ball draws with replacement, bookkeeping, payment) and calls the agent once per decision point.

public_draws_after_round4.researcher_decision_flag: public-draw insertion procedure confirmed verbatim/reported only for a subset of sessions ('sessions 4 and 5'); see audit/missing_information.json

condition_assignment.how_urn_is_chosen: For each period, a fair 6-sided die roll (simulated with a seeded PRNG in task/adapter.py) selects urn A (rolls 1-3) or urn B (rolls 4-6), each with probability 1/2, matching the paper's procedure. The realized urn is held fixed for all 6 rounds within that period and is never shown to the agent during the period -- only revealed in the round-result record after round 6, matching the human procedure of the monitor announcing the true urn at period end.
condition_assignment.how_private_draws_are_generated: Each round, a ball is drawn with replacement from the period's urn using the urn's a:b ball ratio as the draw probability (e.g. baseline symmetric urn A -> P(a)=2/3, P(b)=1/3). This is the single piece of private information given to the agent for that round.
condition_assignment.how_round_order_is_chosen: A random permutation of decision-maker seats (1..6) is drawn once per period (uniformly, matching the paper's colored-marble draw), fixing the order in which rounds occur within the period.
condition_assignment.agent_role_across_a_session: The agent under test plays every decision-maker seat, one at a time and one call at a time -- there is no single continuous human 'self' to imitate across rounds, since in the original study each of the 6 seats was a different, mutually anonymous person who only ever saw their own single private draw. Consequently the adapter does NOT give the agent any memory of a prior round's private draw when calling it for a later round; it only ever passes (a) the current round's own private draw and (b) the public decision history announced so far this period, exactly as a newly-approached human subject would see it.

input_to_agent.condition: one of the condition keys above
input_to_agent.instructions_text: verbatim (study 1) or derived (study 2) oral instructions from materials.json, shown once per session before round 1
input_to_agent.round: integer, 1-6 (this decision-maker's position in this period's random order)
input_to_agent.decisions_so_far_this_period: ordered list of {round, decision} for rounds 1..round-1 of the current period, decision in {'A','B'}
input_to_agent.extra_public_draws: present only under study_1_symmetric/public_draws_after_round4, populated for rounds 5 and 6 with the 2 draws revealed after round 4

output_expected_from_agent.schema_note: task/adapter.py's agent_fn callable must return exactly one of the two strings; adapter.py records it, has the simulated announcer relay it to subsequent rounds, and scores it against the period's true urn once round 6 completes.

session_and_run_structure.unit_of_replication: one 'session' = 1 condition x 15 paid periods x 6 rounds/period = 90 agent calls, matching one human experimental session
session_and_run_structure.full_replication_recommendation: run 3 sessions of baseline_private_draws_only, 3 of public_draws_after_round4, and 6 of asymmetric_urns to mirror the paper's 12-session sample; task/adapter.py exposes n_sessions as a parameter so smaller runs are possible for cheaper/faster smoke-testing
session_and_run_structure.smoke_test: task/adapter.py --smoke-test runs 1 session x 3 periods x 6 rounds per condition using a built-in deterministic baseline policy (no external agent needed) purely to verify the simulation mechanics, JSON I/O, and scoring pipeline execute end-to-end without network access

outputs_consumed_by_evaluation.note: evaluation/evaluation.py consumes exactly this schema (as emitted by task/adapter.py's run_session()) to compute cascade formation rates, efficiency measures, and bias checks against the benchmarks recorded in source/evidence.json.

known_limitations: The adapter cannot reproduce genuine multi-human anonymity/social dynamics (footnote 14's report of subjects using visual/voice cues to detect agonizing decisions); it only reproduces the informational structure of the task.

Practice periods are omitted from the runnable task (they carried no decisions or payment in the original study; see materials.json) -- the agent's very first scored call in a session is period 1 with no prior practice.
study_2_asymmetric's instructions_text is a derived reconstruction, not a verbatim transcript (see audit/missing_information.json).
